facts.name: Greenfall Colony
facts.role: the human settlement — present-tense, alive now
facts.mood: the world has been too kind for too long, and the kindness has started to feel like a hand on the back of the neck
facts.question: welcome guest, pest to be culled, or the next thing being grown?

facts.name: the Tenders
facts.role: colonists who treat the shaping-tools as gifts and farm the way the world seems to want
facts.belief: you do not bite the hand that waters you

facts.name: the Yield Bloc
facts.role: colonists who strip the engineered biosphere for output and keep tripping the unseen alarms
facts.fear: if the world was made, it can be unmade — take while you can

facts.name: the Gardeners
facts.trait: they shape the world by hand and watch the result; you feel the aimed-ness of what they do and the pressure of their attention, but never a body, a ship, or a face
facts.intent: undecided per the colony's reading — stewards, experimenters, breeders, or quarantiners

facts.name: the Loam-Tenders
facts.trait: a lesser hidden caste that keeps the soil-shrines breathing and the gene-looms threaded between the Gardeners' great workings — the maintenance hand of the nursery

facts.name: the First Cultivars
facts.status: harvested or moved on — gone from the surface, present in the soil-record
facts.trait: an earlier lineage the Gardeners grew to mind here before humanity arrived; the precedent the colony is unknowingly repeating

facts.name: the Too-Green Valley
facts.note: soil self-enriches overnight, blights answered before noon — the most AIMED place on the planet, where the colony farms hardest and the Gardeners watch closest

facts.name: the Soil-Record
facts.note: deep strata where the gene-looms have been laying down edits for ages; reading it is reading the Gardeners' lab notebook in living layers

facts.name: the Shrine-Rows
facts.note: ranks of soil-shrines disguised as helpful springs; kneel to tend and you are also being measured

facts.name: the Loom-Hollow
facts.note: where a living gene-loom is still actively threading a lineage — the colony's own, slowly, toward a shape no human chose

facts.name: sensing the aimed-ness
facts.effect: a sensing-one feels when a place is too AIMED — convenience as a tell — and feels the pressure of attention the moment a shaping-tool is used; never sees the Gardener
facts.note: not precognition, not ancestral memory — the felt geometry of intent

facts.tenet: the world is tended; gratitude is the safe posture; greed rings a bell only the watchers hear
the dread that the colony is not the gardener but the garden — the next thing being grown, mid-cultivation, toward an end set elsewhere

facts.name: Maren
facts.role: soil-reader and sensing-one; first to call the valley 'too aimed' out loud

facts.name: Osei
facts.role: loom-warden; tends the gene-loom in the hollow and has started to suspect it is tending him back

facts.name: Vela
facts.role: Yield Bloc engineer who keeps tripping the attention-bells and arguing the alarms are superstition

facts.name: Idris
facts.role: shrine-keeper; believes kneeling at the rows is gratitude, not submission, and is no longer sure of the difference

facts.present_stakes: every shaping-tool the colony uses reveals one more step of the Gardeners' method AND draws their attention; the colony is mid-cultivation and does not yet know toward what; the Yield Bloc and the Tenders pull the world in opposite directions while the watchers score them both
facts.resolves_when: the reveals-chain completes — but the harvest itself is still ahead, unwitnessed, the question still open

facts.title: the harvest the Gardeners are waiting for
facts.state: still unfolding — not a fall, a culmination ahead; what the colony is being grown INTO lies in its future, not the Gardeners' past

facts.title: the first attention-bell rings
facts.note: the day the colony learned, without seeing anyone, that it was being watched

facts.title: the Soil-Record gives up the First Cultivars
facts.note: proof that this soil grew a mind before — and that the mind is gone

facts.name: the Provident Seed
facts.note: makes a place too convenient overnight; arrives where the colony will need it before the colony knows

facts.name: the Living Loom
facts.note: rethreads a lineage thread by thread — patient, reversible, deniable; the pattern answers a hand never in the room

facts.name: the Kneeling Spring
facts.note: a listening-post disguised as a gift to the ground

facts.name: the Threshold Bell
facts.note: rings when greed crosses tending; it does not warn the colony — it summons the watchers

facts.name: the Inherited Key
facts.note: left by the lineage grown before us; it fits a lock the Gardeners built into the living line

facts.name: the Steering-Rod
facts.note: steers the living world a few degrees; using it feels like authorship and is closer to obedience

facts.text: STEP 1 of the Gardeners' method: this world was SEEDED, not found — every convenient trait was placed. The aimed-ness is design, not luck.
STEP 2: a lineage was grown to mind here before us — the First Cultivars — by the same hand. We are not the first crop in this soil.
STEP 3: the tools are instruments, not gifts — using one is the Gardeners reading us, scoring tending against stripping. The bell is the test, not the alarm.
STEP 4: the gene-looms are already editing the colony's own line — slowly, toward a shape no human chose. We are mid-cultivation. We ARE the experiment.
STEP 5, still unfolding: the chain points FORWARD — to a harvest the Gardeners are patiently waiting for. What we are being grown INTO is in our future, not their past.
the rains come on the day the seed needs them; the colony calls it luck and the sensing-ones call it a tell
Osei measured the loom's output against his own children's blood-work and stopped sleeping
the shrines answer prayers no one spoke aloud, which means something heard the unspoken ones
after every bell the world subtly corrects the Bloc's overreach — gently, the way you'd flick a pest off a leaf
the Inherited Key's teeth match a lock found inside the human genome — a lock that was not there at landfall
the First Cultivars left no graves and no war-scars — they were not destroyed; they were taken in
every use of the Steering-Rod is recorded somewhere the colony cannot read — authorship that files a report
the open wager: to use a tool is gratitude, theft, or playing into the plan — and the colony cannot tell which until the harvest
